analysis.title: FX Daily: Dollar holds gains into midterms
key_insights: The dollar is fractionally lower at the start of the week but largely holding recent gains. ING expects DXY to keep trading around 102.00 and sees no strong case for a correction lower.

Betting markets give the Democrats a 70-72% chance of taking both the House and the Senate in the US midterms. ING says a Democratic sweep could argue for a weaker dollar (debt ceiling gridlock, a prolonged government shutdown next year, a more activist foreign policy), but calls those views speculative.
ING cites US macro as the support for the dollar: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% quarter-on-quarter annualised, inflation is above target for a sixth year in a row, and the Fed is readying to tighten again.

This week's US ISM surveys are expected to show continued optimism and high price pressures. Friday's October jobs report is expected to show a modest rebound after a soft September. ING doubts jobs data moves the Fed tightening story unless the report is disastrous, and says price data matters more.

The 9% Nasdaq sell-off last month has softened short-dated US rates. ING sees a further large tech sell-off as probably the biggest risk to long dollar positioning. Apple reports after the close today.
Oil is down 2-3% on reports that Trump wants to let diplomacy with Iran run its course. This reverses Friday's positioning for a fresh attack over the weekend.

Fitch moved its outlook on French sovereign debt from stable to negative late Friday in an unscheduled review, with another review promised by end of February. France is rated A+. The reasons cited are the government's failure to improve public finances amid weak growth. ING thinks this limits EUR/USD rebound potential on softer energy prices.
ING expects more EUR/USD sellers around 1.1200/1250 and expects EUR/CHF to stay pressured toward Friday's lows at 0.9180/85.

The BoE is fully priced for a 25bp hike to 4.00% on Thursday, as high energy prices leave it no alternative. Sterling is also helped by upside UK data surprises, fiscal policy heading in the right direction and warmer ties with the EU. Speculators still run reasonably large short sterling positions, which ING says suggests the outperformance can continue.

EUR/GBP has dropped near 4% in a little over a month. ING expects some consolidation but says it is too early for a significant low, because high energy prices should keep UK rate-hike expectations in place until early next year and French budget problems are unresolved.

In CEE, PMIs have been stagnant or rising since the US-Iran conflict began, showing resilience to the energy shock. Rising energy prices, a stronger dollar and dovish regional central banks should keep pressure on CEE currencies.

ING keeps a dovish bias on CEE this week. EUR/PLN is at 4.400 and could test highs above 4.410 if the NBP is dovish. EUR/CZK is in the 24.300-350 range and could move slightly above 24.350 because the koruna tends to weaken after CNB meetings and 100bp of tightening is already priced.
